hints: Focus on what happens to the N atom, it must replace both Br atoms to close the ring by forming two new C-N bonds.
Notice coniine is a 6-membered ring with 5 carbons plus 1 nitrogen, with a propyl group on the carbon next to N.
Open the ring at the two C-N bonds to get a straight Br to Br chain, then count carbons on each side of the propyl branch to place the Br atoms.
walkthrough:
**See the product as a ring closed by nitrogen**

Coniine is 2-propylpiperidine, a six-membered ring with one $\text{N-H}$ and five carbons. One ring carbon next to N carries $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}\text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{coniine} + 2\text{HBr}$$

**Understand the ring-closing reaction**

Each $\text{C-Br}$ reacts with ammonia by nucleophilic substitution, losing $\text{HBr}$. Two $\text{C-Br}$ bonds become two $\text{C-N}$ bonds to the same N, so X must be an open chain with Br at both ends of the part that becomes the ring.

**Unzip the ring to find X**

Break both $\text{C-N}$ bonds in coniine and put Br back on those two carbons. You get $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

That is 5 carbons between the Br atoms to make a 5 C + 1 N = 6-membered ring, with a $\text{(CH}_2\text{)}_2\text{CH}_3$ propyl group left on the second Br carbon.

**Match to the formula**

Writing it condensed gives $\text{Br(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{CHBr(CH}_2\text{)}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}\text{Br}_2$. This closes neatly to 2-propylpiperidine.

options.A: Incorrect. A cyclopentane cannot open to give the piperidine 6-membered ring, and its formula is $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{14}\text{Br}_2$, not $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}\text{Br}_2$. It also puts both Br on the same carbon, which cannot form two separate C-N bonds to close the observed ring.
options.B: Incorrect. This is also a cyclopentane derivative with formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{14}\text{Br}_2$, so it does not match X. Reaction of a cyclic dibromide with $\text{NH}_3$ would not give the 6-membered coniine skeleton.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{Br(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CHBr(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CH}_3$ has only 4 carbons between the Br atoms, so with N it would close a 5-membered pyrrolidine ring, not a 6-membered piperidine. The side chain would also be butyl, $\text{(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CH}_3$, not propyl.
options.D: Correct. $\text{Br(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{CHBr(CH}_2\text{)}_2\text{CH}_3$ has 5 carbons between the Br positions, giving 5 C + 1 N = 6-membered ring on cyclisation. The $\text{CHBr}$ carbon retains a $\text{(CH}_2\text{)}_2\text{CH}_3$ propyl group, exactly giving 2-propylpiperidine (coniine).
